newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech IPB says foreign issue on hold.
newsitem.headline: Czech IPB says foreign issue on hold.

text.p: A planned foreign equity issue of Czech Investicni a Postovni Banka a.s. (IPB) has been delayed until its board decides whether to complete the issue or make a direct sale of shares to a foriegn investor, the bank said.

Spokesman Jan Rezek told Reuters on Thursday IPB's supervisory board directed management to report by end-October on how to complete the equity expansion, which originally was planned as a minimum of $70-$100 million issue of global depositary receipts preliminarily intended for September.

"There are two possible ways how to prepare foreign (involvement in IPB) -- One way is through the (GDR) issue the other way is the possibility of direct involvement of a foreign investor," Rezek said.
"But nothing has been finally resolved," he added.

Shareholders of IPB, of which the Czech government holds 32.88 percent, in late may approved a two-tiered equity expansion totalling 1.5 billion crowns, calling for a rights issue followed by a GDR issue lead managed by Nomura.
Rezek said that the GDR issue, on which the board was to determine the final timing, was held up for two reasons:

"One thing was that the proportion of the (rights) issue which was originally 1.5 billion crowns. The amount of the shares subscribed came to 1.15 billion crowns, so there was not much left for the GDRs," he said.
"And the second (reason), perhaps indirectly, is the atmosphere around Czech banking," Rezek added.

The Czech banking system was stung by the failure of the medium-sized Kreditni Banka a.s. in August and subsequent central bank forced administration on Agrobanka a.s. because of liquidity problems tied to Kreditni and its investors.

While the central bank has said the four largest banks, with over 70 percent of the country's banking activity, are solid, the Kreditni's politically-charged failure and Agrobanka's illiquidity cast a shadow over the whole sector.
"The question was whether this was the proper time or not for a GDR issue," Rezek said.
IPB is the third largest Czech bank in terms of assets and reported basic capital of 4.6 billion crowns when the equity expansion was approved in May.
Rezek declined further comment on the possible foreign participation in IPB, until board members discussed the way forward.
IPB shares were fixed at 299 crowns on the Prague Stock Exchange on Thursday, one crown lower than Wednesday.
